title: 3D Character Ads: AI Tools or Hiring a Team, and When Each Fits
summary: Decide between AI tools and a hired team for 3D character ads by comparing consistency, revisions, rights and review, with published prices for each route.
body_markdown:
## Who makes 3D character ads for you?


The table covers providers whose published pages describe animation work, as of October 2026. Knowlify is first because it is our top pick for a done-for-you route.


Provider What it makes, as published Published price Turnaround


Knowlify (our top pick for done-for-you) 3D and stylized character animation, alongside AI UGC and AI commercials From $5,000 a month First batch on day 5


[Vidico](https://vidico.com/services/animation-video-production/) 2D and 3D animation, including character animation, voiceover and sound design, for B2B and SaaS teams Monthly plans start around $5,000 a month Not published


[B2W](https://www.b2w.tv/services/animated-commercial-video-production) Animated commercials and social ads for B2B brands, tech startups and cause campaigns Fixed-fee packages from $2,400 for a 60-second video 4 to 6 weeks; 2 to 3 weeks with a rush fee


[Buck](https://buck.co/work) Work filtered by 2D, 3D, character and live action, including animated spots Not published Not published


### Vidico: 2D and 3D animation for B2B and SaaS


Vidico says it produces 2D and 3D animation and motion graphics end to end, including character animation, voiceover and sound design, for B2B and SaaS teams. Its monthly plans start around $5,000 a month, with video, design and animation in one flat fee. It says most B2B explainers cost $5,000 to $12,000 per minute, and that one project can be cut into hooks, ad variations and social posts. Turnaround is not published, so ask for it in writing. Consider it if you are a B2B or SaaS brand.


### B2W: fixed-fee animated commercials with a rush option


B2W sells animated commercials and social ads for B2B brands, tech startups and cause campaigns. Its fixed-fee packages start from $2,400 for a 60-second video, with script, voiceover and sound design included. Square, vertical 9:16 and social cuts come with every project, along with two rounds of revisions at the script, storyboard and animation stages. Most projects take 4 to 6 weeks, or 2 to 3 weeks with a rush fee.


### Buck: check its character work before you brief


Buck describes itself as a talent-driven, global creative company working since 2004. Its work page filters projects by 2D, 3D, character and live action, and includes animated spots for brands. Pricing and turnaround are not published, so ask for a character reel from a similar brand and the names of the people who would direct yours.


## Protecting a character you will use for months


A character you reuse becomes a brand asset, so its rights need the same care as its look. The U.S. Copyright Office's[AI resources](https://www.copyright.gov/ai/) treat digital replicas and copyrightability as separate topics, so route each question to the right reviewer.


In the brief, describe the look as stylized 3D character animation, and ask for original designs rather than replicas of recognizable entertainment characters. Request a rights record for inputs and outputs, not only a statement that the work is AI-generated. Keep the character model, the source files and the approved versions, so the same character can return in a later batch without a redesign.


## Where animated character ads fit on Meta


An animated ad still has to fit its placement. Meta's[video ad guide](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads-guide/video) recommends a 4:5 ratio at 1440 x 1800 pixels for Facebook Feed, and its[Reels ads page](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/facebook-instagram-reels-ads) describes the 9:16 vertical shape, with Reels defaulting to sound on. Build the character for both sizes, and ask whether vertical versions are included or billed extra.


Motion has some evidence behind it. Meta's 2018 post["4 ways to turn still image ads into video ads"](https://www.facebook.com/business/news/4-ways-to-turn-still-image-ads-into-video-ads) says it ran 49 studies with brands using these production methods and saw a positive outcome for 69% of the brands. Those studies compare added motion with still images, not animation with live action, and they date from 2018, so run your own test before you commit a budget. Our[do animated ads work on Meta](https://knowlify.com/articles/do-animated-ads-work-on-meta) guide covers the evidence in more depth.


Meta's[AI transparency update](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/02/gen-ai-transparency-metas-ads-products/) describes labels for photorealistic AI-generated people made with its own tools, and says it will detect ads made with third-party AI tools. The post does not say whether the label rules cover stylized characters, and it does not say third-party detection is live. Ask each provider which tools made each frame.


## Key takeaways


- AI tools suit one simple character that one person can own, direct and review, with the rights record kept in-house.
- Hire a team when the character must hold steady across many ads or needs a documented rights record. Knowlify makes 3D and stylized character animation as a done-for-you service.
- Compare Vidico's monthly plans, B2W's fixed-fee packages and Knowlify's plans from $5,000 a month on output, revisions and rights, not on the first price.
- Build the character for 9:16 and 4:5 placements, and test animation against still images before you scale.


## FAQ


### Are AI-made 3D character ads cheaper than hiring a studio?


The subscription can be, if you reuse the character and have time to direct it. TopView's Plus plan is $36 a month billed annually with 100 credits, while B2W's fixed-fee packages start from $2,400 for a 60-second video and Vidico's plans start around $5,000 a month. The subscription price leaves out your review time and rights record, so compare finished ads, revisions and rights, not only the first price.


### Who owns an AI-generated 3D character?


Ask for a rights record covering the inputs and outputs. The U.S. Copyright Office treats digital replicas and the copyrightability of outputs as separate questions, so ask counsel to confirm your position before you build a campaign around one character.


### How long does a hired 3D character ad take?


B2W says most projects take 4 to 6 weeks from brief to final file, or 2 to 3 weeks with a rush fee. Vidico does not publish a turnaround. Knowlify's first batch arrives on day 5, followed by about 25 finished ads a week.


### Does Meta label animated ads?


Meta says it labels ads with photorealistic AI-generated people made with its own tools, and that it will detect ads made with third-party AI tools and show an "AI info" label. The post does not say third-party detection is live yet, so plan for the label and ask which tools were used.
